newsitem.title: UK: Moody's rates Antenna TV proposed senior notes Ba3.
newsitem.headline: Moody's rates Antenna TV proposed senior notes Ba3.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Tuesday it had assigned a Ba3 debt rating to Antenna TV S.A.'s proposed $100 million issue of senior notes due 2007.
Moody's said this was the first time it had rated the debt of this company.
"The rating reflects Antenna's considerable debt leverage, its rapid development over the last few years and its ambitious future revenue growth plans," Moody's said in a statement.

"Some concerns regarding the company's regulatory environment and currency risk in connection with the notes as well as Antenna's ability, under the terms of the indenture, to incur a meaningful amount of secured debt have also been factored into the rating."
However, Moody's said the rating also recognized Antenna's leading position in the Greek television broadcasting market and its concomitant high share of advertising revenues.

Antenna, in existence since commercial television was introduced to Greece in 1989, is a private company owned by five individuals, including chairman and CEO Minos Kyriakou (25 percent indirect shareholding).
"The CEO divides his time between Antenna and his numerous other business interests, the most important of which is shipping," Moody's said.

"Antenna shares the leading position in overall viewing share (23 percent share in 1996) and advertising revenue (37 percent) with Mega Channel (23 percent/30 percent), a competing general audience programmer, in a relatively fragmented broadcast television market of some 3.2 million TV households.
The rating agency said further competition included four smaller commercial channels, the mainly license-funded state broadcaster, ERT S.A., and a number of unlicensed local channels.

"Antenna's rating strength is underpinned by its commitment to Greek language programming and the high percentage of in-house production : 75 percent of its programming in the 7 a.m. to 1 p.m. time slot (some 5,000 hours per year) is produced in-house," Moody's said.
